title: Private: upgrade step for Optimize config versioning store (migrations + backups) + rollback procedure
author: Michael Nguyen
description:
This PR updates the Private installer upgrade workflow to support the new Optimize config versioning store. It adds an explicit pre-upgrade backup step, runs the required schema migrations, and documents the supported rollback procedure (restore DB backup + disable feature flags) for customer-controlled environments, including air-gapped installs. Motivation: Private customers need immutable config history + one-click rollback, but upgrades must be safe and reversible under enterprise change-management. This PR focuses on the installer-side guarantees (backup, idempotent migrations, and operator guidance) so we can ship config history/rollback in Private without requiring manual DB intervention.

Key changes: (1) Adds an UpgradeStep "optimize_config_versioning_migrate" that (a) verifies DB connectivity/permissions, (b) takes a timestamped logical backup of the control-plane Postgres database (or the configured external DB) before applying migrations, and (c) executes the config-versioning migration bundle with a bounded lock timeout; (2) Introduces installer configuration knobs for backup target location and retention (with sane defaults), and validates free space before attempting the dump; (3) Adds a "Rollback (installer)" doc covering downgrade prerequisites, restoring the snapshot, and re-running the upgrade with versioning disabled; (4) Adds guardrails for offline installs: backup tooling is bundled; no outbound calls; all artifacts must already exist in the upgrade bundle.

Operational notes: Backups are created before any DDL is applied. Migrations are idempotent and are safe to re-run if an upgrade is interrupted. If migration fails after the backup step, the installer stops and surfaces explicit remediation steps (including the restore command). This does not enable any new runtime/console behavior by default; it only ensures the store exists and can be rolled forward/back. Feature enablement remains gated behind the existing Private flags in values/overrides.

Testing: validated on (a) fresh install, (b) upgrade from Private v1.33 -> v1.34 with external Postgres, (c) forced failure mid-migration to confirm backup restore path, (d) air-gapped upgrade bundle execution in staging. See CI results below and manual test notes in the checklist.

Release notes (internal): Private installer now performs automatic backup + migrations for Optimize config versioning store during upgrades; includes documented rollback procedure.

Follow-ups: We should add a small "preflight" subcommand to verify pg_dump/restore permissions and storage capacity without initiating an upgrade (tracked separately).
commits: installer/upgrade: add optimize config versioning migration step
installer/backup: implement pg_dump wrapper with retention + disk checks
docs: add rollback procedure + operator FAQ for air-gapped installs
tests: add upgrade integration test harness for migration idempotency
changed_areas: charts/private/values.yaml (documented flags only; no behavior change by default)
review_conversation:
Connor O'Brien: Can we guarantee the upgrade step fails closed if backup cannot be written? Also, where do we store the backup by default for external DB? Michael Nguyen: Yes, step is now "backup required". For external Postgres, backup is written to the installer host filesystem under /var/lib/redwood/backups by default; operator can override with backup.outputDir. Added explicit error if outputDir is not writable or free space check fails.

Fiona McCarthy: Please confirm we are not including any sensitive config contents in logs. Also we need guidance on retention/redaction (backups can include audit tables). Michael Nguyen: Updated logging to only print backup file path + size, no row counts or SQL output. Docs note backups contain full control-plane DB content and must be stored under customer retention controls; added recommendation to encrypt-at-rest and restrict access. No secret material should be in DB, but we treat backup as sensitive regardless.

Neha Kapoor: What happens if migration takes too long and blocks other services? Add a lock timeout and show clear remediation. Michael Nguyen: Added lock_timeout=30s and statement_timeout=10m for the migration session; if it fails due to lock contention the installer advises to retry during a maintenance window. Also added a note to pause console/admin traffic if the customer has heavy control-plane usage during upgrades.

Benji Okafor: Migration bundle naming should align with control-plane (ENG-4821). Please ensure we match the same versioned migration IDs and don't fork. Michael Nguyen: Confirmed; installer pulls the same embedded migration pack produced by control-plane release artifacts. Added a check that the migration pack version matches the target Private release.

Sean Gallagher: Rollback steps should be "two-command" simple and include a verification check. Michael Nguyen: Docs now include (1) restore command, (2) disable flags, (3) run health check endpoint verification + DB version table check. Added explicit "how to confirm restore worked" section.
related_incidents_or_tickets: SUP-2418 (context: customer latency regression; motivation for rollback)
INT-911 (context: role mappings for on-call rollback; not directly changed here)
checklist: Checklist: - [x] Backup step runs before any migrations - [x] Upgrade fails closed if backup cannot be created - [x] Migrations are idempotent / safe to re-run - [x] Works with external Postgres + in-cluster Postgres - [x] Air-gapped upgrade bundle contains required tooling - [x] Rollback procedure documented and validated in staging - [x] Logs do not print SQL/config payloads - [x] Release train sign-off requested (Connor)
notes_for_release: No default behavior change (flags remain off). Private upgrades to the target version will create a backup and apply schema migrations for the Optimize config versioning store. Operators can rollback by restoring the pre-upgrade DB snapshot and disabling versioning/rollback feature flags.
